'''Vemgo-Mabas''' is an [[Afro-Asiatic language]] of Cameroon and Nigeria. Dialects are Vemgo, Mabas. Blench (2006) considers these to be separate languages. ''Ethnologue'' lists a third dialect, Visik in Nigeria, which is not well attested;<ref name=e18/> Blench suspects it may be a dialect of [[Lamang language|Lamang]] instead.<ref>Blench, 2006. [http://rogerblench.info/Language/Afroasiatic/General/AALIST.pdf The Afro-Asiatic Languages: Classification and Reference List] (ms)</ref>

In Cameroon, Mabas is spoken only in one village on the Nigerian border, namely Mabas village ([[Mokolo]] arrondissement, [[Mayo-Tsanaga]] department, Far North Region) by about 5,000 speakers (ALCAM 1984). Although closely related, Mabas is distinct from [[Hdi language|Hdi]] (78% lexical similarity, 36% mutual intelligibility).<ref name="ALCAM2012">{{cite book|editor-last=Binam Bikoi|editor-first=Charles|date=2012|title=Atlas linguistique du Cameroun (ALCAM)|trans-title=Linguistic Atlas of Cameroon|volume=1: Inventaire des langues|language=fr|location=Yaoundé|publisher=CERDOTOLA|series=Atlas linguistique de l'Afrique centrale (ALAC)|isbn=9789956796069}}</ref>
